title: Beatrix and the Sigil
premise: Juniper Amberdale has spent nine years swallowing poison for King Aldric, building an immunity that keeps him alive and a network of smuggler contacts that keeps him informed. When the old gods stir beneath the Thornfell mountains, Juniper discovers the king's crown is a sigil binding a dead god's hunger to Aldric's living body — and that Beatrix, the court herbalist he loves, has been feeding the sigil with her own memories to keep it dormant. To free the king, one of them must carry the unbinding's cost: the erasure of every memory of the other. In the end, Juniper takes the price himself, and Beatrix must choose between restoring his past or letting him love her again as a stranger.
about_author: Ansel Nystrom is a former apothecary's apprentice from the Yorkshire moors who turned to fantasy after years of cataloguing folk remedies and the superstitions attached to them. He writes in a converted tollhouse, where he claims the previous toll-keeper still argues with him about plot points.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. During a state banquet, Juniper detects henbane in the king's wine but tastes something stranger beneath it — a cold, sweet wrongness no poison manual names. He saves the cup, hides it, and lies to the steward. Emotional beat: the first crack in his certainty that his job is simple survival.

chapters.title: What Beatrix Forgets
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In her herb loft, Beatrix burns a lockbox of letters she can no longer remember writing, each signed with her own hand and addressed to 'the man I must not name.' She feels watched by something old in the castle stones. Emotional beat: grief without a subject, dread taking root.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A scullery maid's prayer to a forgotten river god is answered — literally, catastrophically — flooding the kitchens. Juniper realizes the old gods are waking because the sigil on the crown is weakening. He seeks out Beatrix, the only scholar of old rites left. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, charged proximity.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Using his Thornfell contacts, Juniper trades favors for a smuggler's ledger showing the crown was mined from a god's burial cairn forty years ago. The ledger's last page warns: 'It eats what its bearer loves most.' Emotional beat: cold clarity about the danger, and what it means for Beatrix.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Missing Days
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Confronted, Beatrix confesses: she has been dosing herself with forget-me-not tincture to feed the sigil harmless memories instead of the king's loves. But her supply is nearly gone, and the gaps are widening. Emotional beat: confession as intimacy; love admitted precisely because time is short.

chapters.title: The Road Through Thornfell
chapters.summary: Juniper and Beatrix travel the smuggler roads to the burial cairn seeking the counter-sigil, pursued by the king's captain, who serves the thing in the crown willingly. An avalanche forces them into the god's own tunnels. Emotional beat: trust forged under pursuit; almost-love deferred by duty.

chapters.title: The Cairn Speaks
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the cairn, the dead god's remnant shows them the truth: the unbinding requires a willing vessel to absorb the god's hunger, and the vessel will lose the memories dearest to it. The captain attacks; they escape with the counter-sigil but Beatrix is wounded. Emotional beat: horror at the price, resolve hardening anyway.

chapters.title: Crown of Hunger
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Back at court, the sigil fails mid-audience: the king's body begins consuming itself, courtiers kneeling to something ancient wearing their sovereign's face. Juniper performs the unbinding publicly, drawing the god's hunger into himself before Beatrix can volunteer. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen over consent — love against duty at its cruelest.

chapters.title: The Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The king wakes whole; Juniper lives but looks at her with a stranger's polite blankness. Nine years of shared suppers, arguments, and almosts are gone from him. She holds the antidote tincture that could restore his memories — and reawaken a fragment of the god with them. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh in a single vial.

chapters.title: A New Recipe
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Beatrix chooses not to restore the past but to build a new present: she asks Juniper to taste a dish she's made, the way they once began. He finds the flavor strangely, achingly familiar. Somewhere deep, the buried memories warm but stay quiet. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — memory lost, love chosen again freely.
